We have several networked devices in our house and also several individualized networks configured. Not all of the networks can be seen by all devices so I looked to this Belkin USB WiFi adapter to allow one of the older computer systems to access the most reliable network in the house - a 5GHz network that only one or two of the systems can see.

Installation was a snap. I popped in the CD, told it to install the drivers and we were off to the races. The particular target system was a 32-bit Windows Vista laptop. After just a couple of minutes the driver was completely installed and when I plugged in the USB adapter is was picked up immediately. I could see the desired network as well as several other networks in the neighborhood that were previously invisible to the computer. I shut off the built-in adapter, connected to the 5GHz network and went to the net.

So far, the connection has been very stable and speeds have been excellent. The router to which it is connected is a TP-Link router and so far we have seen no issues between the two devices. I have not had this adapter very long so it is still early to say it’s completely stable but all indicators up to this point have been very favorable.

Several other reviewers have mentioned that this adapter does not work with Linux. This is true - there are no drivers available for this adapter other than for Windows XP/Vista/7/8. If you need an adapter that will allow you to connect a Linux or Mac system to a wireless network, this is not the device you need right now.

So far I can’t find too much about which to complain concerning this router. It seems to be stable and reliable on the system to which it is attached here. I am satisfied with it and based on my experience with it can recommend it - if you’re sticking with Windows.

I got excited to see one of these small portable LED style ones that actually had a decent native resolution (most of them can accept 1080p, but are in reality only 800x600 resolution, or sometimes worse... 640x480!). This one is actually capable of displaying 720p of real dot resolution, which should make it at least as sharp as my Viewsonic and other traditional HD projectors. Ok, perhaps I'm spoiled, but I'm comparing this to our Viewsonic 720p projector that, to be fair cost me 3-4x as much.
And for the most part, it DOES work, however there are some caveats to its use. First of all, it doesn't seem as sharp as my 720p projector, even though it should have the requisite amount of dots. It's OK, its definitely better than the cheap 600p projectors, but something just isn't quite there when comparing side by side. It also doesn't get all that bright, but I suppose that's expected from the LED tech being used. You'll need black out shades or use it only during the night. Then there's the color- it isn't great. It works, but it has a cheap color reproduction that looks kind of flat and lifeless. Dark scenes sort of all blend together and become nearly impossible to see. It lacks the vibrancy of even an inexpensive television from decades ago. It gets the job done, but hardly the "theater experience" if you've been waiting to see that latest action/vfx film the way it was intended. It will look better on your TV at home, the only thing this has going for it is the large projection experience. For example, if you just want to give your kids a backyard movie night and don't care that the color and detail won't be as great as your indoor system, it will do the job on the cheap. I personally would not give up my mid-range projector for this one.
One thing that I found particularly annoying is that rather than the optical zoom and focus dials found on usual projectors, there is only a focus and tilt dial. No zoom. That means you have to physically move the projector closer or further to get it to reach the correct size you are shooting for. That actually got in the way of using it in a couple of specific places my other projectors can be used at optimal sizes.
That's not to say it gets everything wrong- I DO like that it is small and light and can even be turned on it's back to aim at the ceiling. That's something my big projector can't do, due to the airflow and cable management sticking out the rear. It also has a standard 1/4" 20 threaded tripod mounting point, so you can place this onto a tripod and get maximum mounting freedom. That will come in handy as I've always wanted to watch a movie in bed on the ceiling. But otherwise, don't think this projector will be as good as the other mid-rangers out there. This is still very much a low end projector. You'll have to spend at least 2-3x as much to get a decent home theater style experience, and much more if you want a high end one that will handle FHD/4k to get the real deal. This is more of a specialty use item.

There are various reasons why everyone wants to have lighting for camera work. My daughter and I have had a jewelry and pottery business we wanted to start but with everything going berserk two years ago, we put a hold on it all.

In the meanwhile, my perfect light that I love which goes on my camera shorted out. That made me frustrated. This light is larger, but I figured I can set it up on a tripod.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a box with a foam liner. There is a Type C connector for charging , a cord, and a screw on adapter for a tripod or on top of a camera if your camera can handle it.

CHARGING
This took me a while to charge it. After I left it in overnight, this was fully charged.

BATTERY
I purposely charged this up and did not use it for a few months. This battery was still up near 10 hours at 10% lighting on 5600K when I started it up. That is a great power retention. Using it, I get a few hours out of it before I recharge and I use it at less than 50% usually.

LIGHT COLOR
For all of the colors provided by this light, they are great. What I got it for, however, was jewelry and pottery photos so I am not going to be using the RGB lights very much except for advertising photos perhaps.

WHITE LIGHT COLOR
The white light color is kind of frustrating for me. I like to have natural lighting that does not add color to the photos. That means that in my situation, anything above 50% is too bright. This light only goes to 5600K in cool tones, but when I use it under 50% it still has some green/yellow to it. Yes, I can edit it out with color adjustments in my software, but it is a bit frustrating.

Some photos work out well, but others not so much. I do like a bit of yellow in my photos, so I will pull it down a little bit toward lower K value if I want warmer tones (aka sunlight type)

CONTROLS
The controls are easy to use and I like that it is mechanical and not software driven. The battery left is shown clearly and the settings are also lit up well.

WEIGHT
This is a heavy light. It is twice the size and weight of my other light so I can not put it on my camera. I use a tripod instead.

CASE
This does not come with a hard case which disappoints me. It has a cheap velveteen bag with no padding. It is nice, but you will need a case to keep this in for protection along with your camera.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This light is not bad. It give me some settings to work with on my jewelry. I would like it better if it was just a bit cooler in capability (higher K). As it is, I use it, but sometimes I find myself adding other lights to balance out the tint of this one.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. This is nice, has nice battery capacity and retention of charge, but the light white color is not quite as nice as I was hoping for. It still is decent and I use it.

I'll be honest, I was expecting this to be another cheap off-brand mouse. I'm pleasantly surprised at how good it is- It looks pretty great, and rather than being covered in shiny fingerprint-magnet plastic like most cheap mice, a majority of the surface is textured (almost like a rubberized plastic). The USB receiver fits inside the body of the mouse for storage, which is great for travelling with it as I do. I've owned other mice that did that before too (an old Logitech), but unlike that old Logitech, this one uses a built-in rechargeable battery. To be honest, my Logitech mouse was great but after a couple of years the battery started making a bad connection inside (corroded contacts were keeping the battery from working), so I'd have to try to clean it off every few uses on the road to keep it working. With this product however, it seems less likely that will become a problem. Also, the ability to plug it in and charge it off the computer directly if it starts to die is a great plus!
My first impression was that the mouse was a little jumpier than I expected, but then I noticed the little button under the scroll wheel and discovered that it was for changing the DPI. Honestly, I'm not sure why they put it in such an easy to use spot, I feel like this isn't something that needs to change very often. But a couple of clicks on that button got me to about the mouse speed I like. I'm actually really happy with this product and although I was shopping around for a replacement Logitech, I think I'll keep this one in my travel bag instead!
